title: Changing Mindsets
coreMove: Mindset changes through repeated interpretation and action: notice the fixed voice, understand its fear, choose a learning plan, and maintain the practice.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a harsh thought could stop revision
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Aaron Beck and cognitive therapy to notice and answer extreme judgments

exampleSpecs.stakes: a conceptual shift must become action
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use mindset lectures with college students to connect new interpretation to a concrete study plan

exampleSpecs.domain: district intervention planning for ninth graders
exampleSpecs.stakes: study skills may sound empty without a belief in change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use adolescent mindset workshop to compare study skills alone with skills plus brain-growth explanation

exampleSpecs.stakes: students may treat repetition as punishment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Brainology to make neurons, connections, and practice concrete

exampleSpecs.audience: adults whose fixed response protects identity
exampleSpecs.stakes: attacking the fixed voice may deepen resistance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Karen Horney and Carl Rogers to treat the fixed persona with compassion and direction

exampleSpecs.domain: software team retrospectives after initial improvement
exampleSpecs.audience: teams whose first mindset shift fades
exampleSpecs.stakes: old defensive habits may return after early relief
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: anchor in true growth mindset and maintenance after initial change
